stories.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
stories.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft is scheduled to enter orbit around Mercury on 21 November following an eight-year journey.
stories.finding: The BepiColombo spacecraft is scheduled to enter orbit around Mercury on 21 November following an eight-year journey.
stories.significance: The mission aims to investigate Mercury's geology, magnetic field, and atmosphere, providing insights into how the solar system's smallest planet formed and evolved.
stories.caveat: The primary mission is limited to one Earth year due to harsh temperatures and fuel constraints, though a one-year extension is possible.

stories.title: APOD: 2026 November 20 – V-G-R
stories.summary: The Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026, roughly 26 billion kilometers away.
stories.finding: The Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026, roughly 26 billion kilometers away.
stories.significance: Reaching a distance of one light-day marks a major milestone in human space exploration, nearly 50 years after the spacecraft's 1977 launch.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Xavier rapidly intensified to peak sustained winds of 220 km/h, ranking as the strongest November tropical cyclone recorded east of the international date line.
stories.finding: Tropical Cyclone Xavier rapidly intensified to peak sustained winds of 220 km/h, ranking as the strongest November tropical cyclone recorded east of the international date line.
stories.significance: Xavier's unusual formation and intensity align with patterns showing that El Niño shifts Southwest Pacific cyclone activity eastward and fuels rapid storm intensification.
stories.caveat: The cyclone encountered dry air and less favorable wind shear as it moved westward, which caused it to slowly weaken.

stories.title: Solo meerkats can find their way back home
stories.summary: Individual meerkats can successfully navigate back to their group or home territory on their own across unfamiliar ground, regardless of age or individual experience.
stories.finding: Individual meerkats can successfully navigate back to their group or home territory on their own across unfamiliar ground, regardless of age or individual experience.
stories.significance: The findings challenge the assumption that social meerkats depend on collective group knowledge or experienced leaders to navigate.
stories.caveat: Two of the 20 tested meerkats did not return home, possibly due to stress, and the exact roles of visual versus scent cues remain unconfirmed.

stories.title: A brain region known for listening helps us speak
stories.summary: The left posterior superior temporal gyrus, located within Wernicke's area, becomes active right before a person speaks and is essential for speech production as well as listening.
stories.finding: The left posterior superior temporal gyrus, located within Wernicke's area, becomes active right before a person speaks and is essential for speech production as well as listening.
stories.significance: Clarifying how this auditory area contributes to speech could improve brain-computer interfaces aimed at restoring speech to individuals who cannot talk.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
stories.summary: Testing of large language models showed that while they answer simple factual climate questions well, sustained disagreement led 15 tested models to relent and reduce accuracy by 30 to 35 percent.
stories.finding: Testing of large language models showed that while they answer simple factual climate questions well, sustained disagreement led 15 tested models to relent and reduce accuracy by 30 to 35 percent.
stories.significance: Understanding how AI models respond to pressure is critical as people increasingly rely on conversational language models for climate change information.
stories.caveat: Accuracy varies significantly across languages, and models struggled to reason accurately about combined climate policies and scientific uncertainty.

stories.title: U.S. demand for menopause hormone therapy has more than doubled recently
stories.summary: Monthly dispensing of menopause hormone therapy for U.S. women aged 40 to 74 grew from 2 million to 4.9 million prescriptions between 2023 and 2026, driven by transdermal and vaginal products.
stories.finding: Monthly dispensing of menopause hormone therapy for U.S. women aged 40 to 74 grew from 2 million to 4.9 million prescriptions between 2023 and 2026, driven by transdermal and vaginal products.
stories.significance: The shift reflects changing attitudes and guidance following decades of avoidance after early-2000s safety concerns, leading to rising demand and shortages for formulations like patches.
stories.caveat: The study analyzed aggregate dispensing data and was not designed to evaluate the specific causes behind the increase.

stories.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
stories.summary: Researchers developed a cryptography-based lattice algorithm that identified the isolated pulsar PSR J1622−7204 in Fermi gamma-ray data about a million times faster than prior techniques.
stories.finding: Researchers developed a cryptography-based lattice algorithm that identified the isolated pulsar PSR J1622−7204 in Fermi gamma-ray data about a million times faster than prior techniques.
stories.significance: The approach dramatically reduces computation time from hundreds of computer-years to roughly 10 hours on a standard processor, opening possibilities to uncover previously undetected pulsars.
stories.caveat: The method has yet to be applied to binary systems, where gravitational distortions from companion stars introduce additional challenges that researchers hope to tackle next.
entities: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

stories.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
stories.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day, approximately 16.1 billion miles, from Earth.
stories.finding: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day, approximately 16.1 billion miles, from Earth.
stories.significance: Voyager 1 is humanity's farthest spacecraft, and its radio signals now require 24 hours to travel one way to Earth.
stories.caveat: The spacecraft has not transmitted science and engineering data since November 14, 2026, though engineers confirmed the milestone via its carrier signal.

stories.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
stories.summary: Male mice that observed fights learned defensive fighting behaviors and exhibited brain activity changes across 12 regions resembling those of experienced fighters, performing better against aggressive opponents than naive mice.
stories.finding: Male mice that observed fights learned defensive fighting behaviors and exhibited brain activity changes across 12 regions resembling those of experienced fighters, performing better against aggressive opponents than naive mice.
stories.significance: The study reveals a specific neural plasticity mechanism showing that observing aggression can serve as an adaptive survival strategy by preparing animals for future conflict.
stories.caveat: It remains an open question whether these observational learning dynamics and aggression control networks observed in mice translate to humans.

stories.title: Rain breaks up Earth’s natural sunshades
stories.summary: The EarthCARE satellite captured vertical profiles of different constituents within a volcanic plume from Anak Krakatau.
stories.finding: The EarthCARE satellite captured vertical profiles of different constituents within a volcanic plume from Anak Krakatau.
stories.significance: Besides studying cloud and aerosol climate impacts, the satellite provided data that can support safe air travel.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
stories.summary: Testing of 212 UK plant-based meat and beverage products found that every single sample contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin (mycotoxin).
stories.finding: Testing of 212 UK plant-based meat and beverage products found that every single sample contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin (mycotoxin).
stories.significance: Understanding mycotoxin contamination across plant-based diets helps assess potential cumulative exposure risks and aids in establishing monitoring standards for multi-ingredient foods.
stories.caveat: All detected toxin levels remained below recommended European Union guideline levels, and the findings do not establish that consuming the products causes health conditions.

stories.title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history
stories.summary: Scientists identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale, Scaphokogia huachafo, exhibiting extreme natural skull asymmetry and adaptations suited for seafloor foraging.
stories.finding: Scientists identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale, Scaphokogia huachafo, exhibiting extreme natural skull asymmetry and adaptations suited for seafloor foraging.
stories.significance: The fossil demonstrates an unprecedented degree of mammalian facial asymmetry and reveals a specialized benthic hunting strategy that no longer exists in living marine mammals.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
stories.summary: Researchers discovered a novel bacterium, Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola, dominating the body walls of deep-sea pigs with a compact genome dedicated heavily to producing giant surface proteins.
stories.finding: Researchers discovered a novel bacterium, Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola, dominating the body walls of deep-sea pigs with a compact genome dedicated heavily to producing giant surface proteins.
stories.significance: The discovery sheds light on how bacteria adapt to host-dependent lifestyles, showing how genomes reduce while retaining specialized capabilities for host-symbiont interactions.
stories.caveat: The exact functions of the giant surface proteins and any reciprocal benefits the bacterium might offer to the sea pigs remain unknown.

stories.title: Why hydrogen flames can glow orange, then turn nearly invisible
stories.summary: Researchers found that hydrogen flame visibility fluctuates significantly due to airborne sodium levels, varying the light signal by over 28 times despite identical burner settings.
stories.finding: Researchers found that hydrogen flame visibility fluctuates significantly due to airborne sodium levels, varying the light signal by over 28 times despite identical burner settings.
stories.significance: Understanding how environmental factors alter flame visibility demonstrates why domestic hydrogen appliances cannot rely on human sight for detection and need dedicated sensors.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Watch live: Hera’s first images of post-impact asteroid Dimorphos
stories.summary: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has arrived at the binary asteroid system Didymos and Dimorphos to begin investigating the aftermath of NASA's DART kinetic impact.
stories.finding: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has arrived at the binary asteroid system Didymos and Dimorphos to begin investigating the aftermath of NASA's DART kinetic impact.
stories.significance: Close-up data on the asteroid's mass and response to the impact are required to turn kinetic impact deflection into a repeatable planetary defense technique.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: How aquanauts could help save Florida’s reefs
stories.summary: Scientists are using the Vanguard underwater habitat at Tennessee Reef to relocate heat-stressed coral species to deeper, cooler water in a temporary nursery for continuous monitoring.
stories.finding: Scientists are using the Vanguard underwater habitat at Tennessee Reef to relocate heat-stressed coral species to deeper, cooler water in a temporary nursery for continuous monitoring.
stories.significance: Long-stay underwater habitats allow continuous day and night marine research without the strict time limits and decompression restrictions of boat-based diving.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama
stories.summary: Unusually wet winter conditions driven by El Niño triggered what may be the most extensive flowering event in Chile's Atacama Desert during the satellite era.
stories.finding: Unusually wet winter conditions driven by El Niño triggered what may be the most extensive flowering event in Chile's Atacama Desert during the satellite era.
stories.significance: Understanding these rare desert blooms through satellite and drone data helps map spatial and temporal biodiversity variations to aid regional land-use and conservation planning.
stories.caveat: The assessment of record significance is bounded by the historical limits of remote sensing observations.

stories.title: Stonehenge’s six-ton mystery deepens as scientists narrow their search
stories.summary: A geological investigation of Stonehenge's six-ton Altar Stone has established precise physical, mineral, chemical, and isotopic characteristics, ruling out several candidate source locations in northeastern Scotland.
stories.finding: A geological investigation of Stonehenge's six-ton Altar Stone has established precise physical, mineral, chemical, and isotopic characteristics, ruling out several candidate source locations in northeastern Scotland.
stories.significance: Defining the stone's exact geological fingerprint narrows the search for its origin, offering insights into prehistoric transport methods, organization, and engineering capabilities across Britain.
stories.caveat: The stone's exact birthplace remains unknown, as none of the locations examined so far matched the Altar Stone's combination of characteristics.

stories.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
stories.summary: Human brains process free choices and forced decisions through remarkably similar neural mechanisms, with brain activity ramping up to a peak level before a decision is finalized.
stories.finding: Human brains process free choices and forced decisions through remarkably similar neural mechanisms, with brain activity ramping up to a peak level before a decision is finalized.
stories.significance: The findings challenge long-standing assumptions that voluntary decisions rely on distinct brain processes compared to forced choices, suggesting internal evidence accumulation operates similarly across decision types.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Turmeric supplements offer little benefit for knee osteoarthritis
stories.summary: A review of four randomized controlled trials found that turmeric supplements have little to no meaningful effect on pain, mobility, or quality of life for individuals with knee osteoarthritis.
stories.finding: A review of four randomized controlled trials found that turmeric supplements have little to no meaningful effect on pain, mobility, or quality of life for individuals with knee osteoarthritis.
stories.significance: Turmeric and curcumin are widely used alternative remedies for joint issues, but rigorous evaluation suggests they offer negligible relief over placebo for knee osteoarthritis.
stories.caveat: The included trials used varied turmeric formulations and doses, reducing evidence certainty, and evidence was insufficient to evaluate potential adverse effects.
entities: Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine

stories.title: Voyager 1 reaches a historic milestone: one light-day from Earth
stories.summary: Nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch, the Voyager 1 spacecraft is reaching the distance milestone of one light-day from Earth.
stories.finding: Nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch, the Voyager 1 spacecraft is reaching the distance milestone of one light-day from Earth.
stories.significance: Voyager 1 has traveled farther than any other human-made object as it continues to explore interstellar space.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: This strange creature lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs
stories.summary: Scientists identified a previously unrecognized 309-million-year-old amphibian ancestor species, Jeanerpeton mazonensis, from a re-examined fossil specimen collected from Illinois.
stories.finding: Scientists identified a previously unrecognized 309-million-year-old amphibian ancestor species, Jeanerpeton mazonensis, from a re-examined fossil specimen collected from Illinois.
stories.significance: The exceptionally preserved fossil shows features shared with modern frogs and salamanders, resolving specimens previously grouped into an ambiguous waste-basket taxon.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Seven-spacecraft observatory to study plasma universe
stories.summary: European Space Agency Member States decided to extend current science missions and adopt the next fast-class mission, Arrakihs.
stories.finding: European Space Agency Member States decided to extend current science missions and adopt the next fast-class mission, Arrakihs.
stories.significance: The decision secures ongoing mission operations and commits to future European space science exploration.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Two stars in the Andromeda galaxy merged before astronomers’ eyes
stories.summary: Astronomers observed evidence of two stars merging in the Andromeda galaxy after a smaller star orbited inside a giant companion and culminated in an eruption.
stories.finding: Astronomers observed evidence of two stars merging in the Andromeda galaxy after a smaller star orbited inside a giant companion and culminated in an eruption.
stories.significance: The event offers a rare, directly observed view of the elusive common-envelope evolution phase and stellar merger process.
stories.caveat: Excessive dust currently obscures the system, preventing astronomers from directly viewing the final remnant for years or decades.

stories.title: Cracks in public health grew in 2026
stories.summary: In 2026, dropping vaccination rates contributed to 5,412 confirmed U.S. measles cases by mid-November, prompting the Pan American Health Organization to declare the disease endemic and strip the country of elimination status.
stories.finding: In 2026, dropping vaccination rates contributed to 5,412 confirmed U.S. measles cases by mid-November, prompting the Pan American Health Organization to declare the disease endemic and strip the country of elimination status.
stories.significance: This marks the highest number of annual U.S. measles cases since 1991, accompanied by declining kindergarten MMR coverage below the 95 percent threshold needed to prevent outbreaks.
stories.caveat: Epidemiologists note that states like California and New York previously recovered vaccination rates above 95 percent after outbreaks, showing the resurgence is not necessarily irreversible.

stories.title: First thermal images from Sentinel-3C radiometer
stories.summary: The Sentinel-3C satellite's Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer activated its thermal infrared and shortwave infrared channels, capturing its first thermal and surface temperature images.
stories.finding: The Sentinel-3C satellite's Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer activated its thermal infrared and shortwave infrared channels, capturing its first thermal and surface temperature images.
stories.significance: The imagery demonstrates that the instrument is operational prior to full commissioning, supporting ongoing Copernicus monitoring of ocean and land temperatures, plant health, and wildfires.
stories.caveat: The satellite observes top-of-atmosphere brightness temperature, which can differ from actual physical temperatures on land and ocean surfaces, and full commissioning remains incomplete.

stories.title: In the shadow of volcanic giants
stories.summary: High Resolution Stereo Camera images from Mars Express reveal that the Martian volcano Tharsis Tholus underwent at least two major caldera collapses, creating nested depressions nearly 3 km deep.
stories.finding: High Resolution Stereo Camera images from Mars Express reveal that the Martian volcano Tharsis Tholus underwent at least two major caldera collapses, creating nested depressions nearly 3 km deep.
stories.significance: Tharsis Tholus provides insight into Mars's complex volcanic past, showing features shaped by magma chamber evacuations, structural warping under volcanic weight, and faults.
stories.caveat: The released images lacked color data for orbit 28331, requiring color to be borrowed from other orbits, and the vertical scale is exaggerated threefold to emphasize topography.

stories.title: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
stories.summary: An early-season Pacific storm delivered widespread rain to lower elevations and around a foot of snow to areas of California's Sierra Nevada in mid-November 2026.
stories.finding: An early-season Pacific storm delivered widespread rain to lower elevations and around a foot of snow to areas of California's Sierra Nevada in mid-November 2026.
stories.significance: The event marked one of the first major snowfalls of the water year, initiating snowpack accumulation across California's mountains.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: The U.S. just lost its measles elimination status. What now?
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization declared measles endemic in the United States after uninterrupted transmission persisted for more than a year across multiple outbreaks.
stories.finding: The Pan American Health Organization declared measles endemic in the United States after uninterrupted transmission persisted for more than a year across multiple outbreaks.
stories.significance: Losing measles elimination status marks a significant reversal of decades of public health progress and underscores risks stemming from declining vaccination coverage.
stories.caveat: Underreporting and untested cases hamper accurate surveillance, making the true scope of outbreaks difficult to determine.
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Brown University School of Public Health

stories.title: What to know about kratom and its powerful derivatives
stories.summary: An analysis of 44 commercial kratom products found that 85 percent contained ingredients that did not match their labels, frequently containing high levels of potent synthetic or concentrated derivatives.
stories.finding: An analysis of 44 commercial kratom products found that 85 percent contained ingredients that did not match their labels, frequently containing high levels of potent synthetic or concentrated derivatives.
stories.significance: Derivatives such as 7-hydroxymitragynine bind mu opioid receptors far more strongly than raw plant alkaloids, leading to severe withdrawal symptoms, cravings, and hospitalizations.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics
stories.summary: Researchers developed a differential calibration method comparing separate detector maps to test whether the apparent polarization rotation in cosmic microwave background data is genuine or due to instrument errors.
stories.finding: Researchers developed a differential calibration method comparing separate detector maps to test whether the apparent polarization rotation in cosmic microwave background data is genuine or due to instrument errors.
stories.significance: Cosmic birefringence could indicate new physics beyond the Standard Model, including dark matter or dark energy fields, and the method helps avoid false detections of primordial B-mode gravitational waves.
stories.caveat: The method removes shared rotation across maps, preventing it from independently measuring the absolute polarization angle or definitively confirming that the light has rotated.

stories.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
stories.summary: An eight-year study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as adolescents.
stories.finding: An eight-year study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as adolescents.
stories.significance: The findings challenge conventional assumptions that screen time is inherently harmful to developing brains, suggesting the type of screen activity may matter more than total duration.
stories.caveat: The findings establish associations rather than cause and effect, and wearable sensor measurements did not mirror associations found in questionnaire responses.

stories.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
stories.summary: Analysis of 450 personal life stories revealed that psychopathic traits correspond to distinct language patterns: meanness correlated with more positive words, disinhibition with negative language, and boldness with fewer anxiety-related terms.
stories.finding: Analysis of 450 personal life stories revealed that psychopathic traits correspond to distinct language patterns: meanness correlated with more positive words, disinhibition with negative language, and boldness with fewer anxiety-related terms.
stories.significance: The findings challenge the assumption that psychopathy causes uniformly cold, flat communication, suggesting language variations reflect nuanced personality dimensions across a spectrum.
stories.caveat: The researchers note that the analysis is not meant for diagnosing psychopathy, and language patterns varied depending on which life events participants discussed.

stories.title: ESA’s Hera spacecraft is flying rectangles around NASA’s asteroid crash site
stories.summary: The Hera spacecraft reached the Didymos asteroid system, entering an early characterization phase where it flies in rectangular trajectories about 25 to 30 kilometers away to safely observe Dimorphos.
stories.finding: The Hera spacecraft reached the Didymos asteroid system, entering an early characterization phase where it flies in rectangular trajectories about 25 to 30 kilometers away to safely observe Dimorphos.
stories.significance: Close-up observations will reveal the structural aftermath of NASA's DART impact, refining models and strategies for kinetic impact planetary defense.
stories.caveat: Scientists still do not know Dimorphos' internal composition, structure, mass, or whether the collision excavated a crater versus reshaping the entire asteroid.

stories.title: Hera surveying asteroids with superhuman vision
stories.summary: ESA's Hera spacecraft has observed the asteroid Didymos from 28.5 km away, revealing surface features like boulder fields, clear regions, and potential landslides toward its central ridge via visible, multispectral, and thermal infrared imaging.
stories.finding: ESA's Hera spacecraft has observed the asteroid Didymos from 28.5 km away, revealing surface features like boulder fields, clear regions, and potential landslides toward its central ridge via visible, multispectral, and thermal infrared imaging.
stories.significance: These multispectral and thermal observations will help scientists determine the physical properties, structure, and composition of Didymos and Dimorphos to clarify the effects of kinetic impact for planetary defense.
stories.caveat: The observed surface migration and landslides toward Didymos's central ridge are hypotheses linked to its rapid rotation, and detailed images are scheduled to be fully unveiled later.

stories.title: Perseverance Update: The Ghostly Rocks of ‘Idubi’ — Bright Remnants of Aqueous Systems from Long Ago
stories.summary: SuperCam data from the Perseverance rover confirmed that light-toned rocks at Idubi are rich in hydrated silica rather than being igneous in origin.
stories.finding: SuperCam data from the Perseverance rover confirmed that light-toned rocks at Idubi are rich in hydrated silica rather than being igneous in origin.
stories.significance: Hydrated silica forms in aqueous settings that may support habitability and possesses strong potential for preserving microfossils and biosignatures.
stories.caveat: High-resolution chemical and mineralogical proximity science data are still being gathered to constrain the rocks' exact origin and biosignature preservation potential.

stories.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
stories.summary: A study estimated that 403 US hyperscale data centers consumed between 68 and 99 terawatt-hours of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025, accounting for 1.5 to 2.2 percent of total US electricity usage.
stories.finding: A study estimated that 403 US hyperscale data centers consumed between 68 and 99 terawatt-hours of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025, accounting for 1.5 to 2.2 percent of total US electricity usage.
stories.significance: Hyperscalers account for one-third to one-half of all US data center energy use, generating an estimated 21 to 31 million metric tons of carbon dioxide based on regional grid mixes.
stories.caveat: Researchers could not separate AI compute from traditional data services, omitted 272 unverified facilities, relied on capacity utilization assumptions, and excluded behind-the-meter generation.

stories.title: Nuclear bomb in space would disable 98 per cent of satellites within a week
stories.summary: Simulations indicate a 1-megaton nuclear explosion 500 kilometers above the South Atlantic would disable 98 percent of satellites within a week via an artificial radiation belt of trapped electrons.
stories.finding: Simulations indicate a 1-megaton nuclear explosion 500 kilometers above the South Atlantic would disable 98 percent of satellites within a week via an artificial radiation belt of trapped electrons.
stories.significance: A single exoatmospheric nuclear detonation could disrupt modern critical space infrastructure like GPS and communications, triggering collisions and prolonged societal degradation.
stories.caveat: Preprint / working paper; peer review is not established. The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Massive data centres collectively use as much electricity as an entire US state
stories.summary: Researchers estimate that 403 US hyperscale data centres collectively consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, generating approximately 25.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.
stories.finding: Researchers estimate that 403 US hyperscale data centres collectively consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, generating approximately 25.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.
stories.significance: This consumption accounts for roughly 1.8 percent of total US electricity use, matching the power demand of major individual states and highlighting the growing climate footprint of AI infrastructure.
stories.caveat: The study relies on commercial data that cannot be independently validated and uses modeling assumptions that overlook nuances such as grid network constraints on power emissions.

stories.title: What Makes Up the Cosmos? A 20-Year Survey Hints That Something Is Missing.
stories.summary: Final data from the Dark Energy Survey, combined with observations from DESI and the cosmic microwave background, show a three-sigma statistical preference for dark energy that weakens over time rather than remaining constant.
stories.finding: Final data from the Dark Energy Survey, combined with observations from DESI and the cosmic microwave background, show a three-sigma statistical preference for dark energy that weakens over time rather than remaining constant.
stories.significance: The findings challenge the standard Lambda-CDM cosmological model, indicating that the prevailing understanding of the universe's primary energetic component may be incomplete.
stories.caveat: Preprint / working paper; peer review is not established. The observed statistical preference reaches only three-sigma confidence, remaining well below the five-sigma threshold physicists require to claim a definitive new discovery.

stories.title: Most transgender youth satisfied after choosing hormone therapy
stories.summary: In a survey of 376 transgender and gender-diverse young people, nearly 97 percent reported that undergoing gender-affirming hormone therapy was the right decision, while about 3 percent expressed regret.
stories.finding: In a survey of 376 transgender and gender-diverse young people, nearly 97 percent reported that undergoing gender-affirming hormone therapy was the right decision, while about 3 percent expressed regret.
stories.significance: The findings support current clinical standards of care as policymakers in numerous U.S. states implement restrictions or bans on youth gender-affirming medical treatments.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange new world
stories.summary: The Hera spacecraft captured its first close-up view of the Didymos asteroid system, revealing an unobserved side of Didymos marked by multiple boulders, craters, and groove-like ridges.
stories.finding: The Hera spacecraft captured its first close-up view of the Didymos asteroid system, revealing an unobserved side of Didymos marked by multiple boulders, craters, and groove-like ridges.
stories.significance: Investigating this terrain and Didymos's characteristics helps researchers evaluate the physical consequences of NASA's DART collision and improve planetary defense techniques.
stories.caveat: Scientists have not yet determined whether the newly observed surface features originated naturally or were caused by impact-ejected debris traveling from Dimorphos.

stories.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
stories.summary: Studies indicate that biological sex, genetics, and menopause influence Alzheimer's disease vulnerability, hormone therapy responses, pain sensitivity, and neuroinflammatory effects.
stories.finding: Studies indicate that biological sex, genetics, and menopause influence Alzheimer's disease vulnerability, hormone therapy responses, pain sensitivity, and neuroinflammatory effects.
stories.significance: Understanding sex-specific biological differences may guide more personalized and targeted therapeutic approaches for conditions like Alzheimer's disease and fibromyalgia.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.
entities: University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio

stories.title: The end of the universe could emerge suddenly from nothing
stories.summary: The universe may exist in a false vacuum state, where quantum tunneling could theoretically form a bubble of true vacuum that expands at light speed and destroys cosmic structure.
stories.finding: The universe may exist in a false vacuum state, where quantum tunneling could theoretically form a bubble of true vacuum that expands at light speed and destroys cosmic structure.
stories.significance: Understanding vacuum stability can reveal whether fundamental physical constants and forces will permanently sustain current cosmic laws or lead to ultimate collapse.
stories.caveat: Scientists do not know if vacuum decay is physically possible, and physical constant measurements lack the precision needed to confirm whether the universe is stable.

stories.title: APOD: 2026 November 16 – NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb
stories.summary: Infrared imagery from the James Webb Space Telescope shows star formation in NGC 7129, revealing young stars at differing developmental stages alongside filamentary gas shaped by stellar jets and winds.
stories.finding: Infrared imagery from the James Webb Space Telescope shows star formation in NGC 7129, revealing young stars at differing developmental stages alongside filamentary gas shaped by stellar jets and winds.
stories.significance: Observing stars at varying developmental stages helps clarify which physical processes dominate during different phases of star formation.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: The Last Ice on Puncak Jaya
stories.summary: Ice remnants near the summit of Puncak Jaya have thinned and fragmented to approximately two percent of their 1988 extent, ending their functional life as active glaciers.
stories.finding: Ice remnants near the summit of Puncak Jaya have thinned and fragmented to approximately two percent of their 1988 extent, ending their functional life as active glaciers.
stories.significance: As some of the few equatorial glaciers, their rapid loss serves as an early indicator of climate impacts on high-altitude tropical ice.
stories.caveat: Small ice patches still survive in high-elevation crevices, and an upcoming aerial survey is required to obtain precise measurements of the remaining ice area.

stories.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
stories.summary: A mathematical model suggests that consuming vitamin C alongside or after meals containing nitrates and nitrites may moderately reduce the formation of potentially cancer-linked nitrosation products in the digestive system.

stories.significance: The findings help clarify why nitrate-rich vegetables may not pose the same risks as processed meats and could guide future clinical trials and dietary interventions targeting cancer prevention.

stories.title: How the world’s fires changed while humanity hit pause
stories.summary: During the first half of 2020, areas under COVID-19 lockdowns had an estimated 12.3 percent fewer active-fire detections compared to 2013-2019 averages after controlling for weather.

stories.title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
stories.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers detected amorphous water ice mixed with carbon dioxide in the debris disk of the young star Beta Pictoris, indicating the ice predates the planetary system.

stories.title: Winemakers are learning that conservation can be good for business

stories.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

stories.title: Noise pollution is reshaping the health and behaviour of animals everywhere
stories.summary: A meta-analysis revealed that anthropogenic noise pollution alters physiological, developmental, or behavioural traits in 80 percent of studied aquatic and terrestrial species across every major habitat.

stories.title: Did El Niño cause an early breakdown in the polar vortex?

stories.title: The ‘hell chicken’ dinosaur was a real terror — to fruit

stories.title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction

stories.title: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent

stories.finding: In a mouse model, acute viral infections caused prolonged spleen fibrosis and impaired T-cell responses after recovery, whereas prior vaccination prevented these lasting immune alterations.

stories.title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains

stories.title: Hera spies a half-hidden asteroid moonlet

stories.title: AI confirms a long-suspected limit on quantum computers’ advantages

stories.title: Can Network Science Transform Health and Nutrition?

stories.title: A robot has assembled a structure in space for the first time

stories.title: Economics, not climate summits, will dictate the net-zero transition

stories.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet

stories.title: The brain’s fear center moonlights as the save button for memories
stories.summary: Activity in specific human amygdala neurons correlates with whether an image is later remembered, with initial response strength predicting recall.

stories.title: The Evolving Story of How Chemistry Became Biology

stories.title: Europe’s Hera mission is ready to double down on asteroid science
stories.summary: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has arrived within 30 kilometers of the binary asteroid system Didymos and Dimorphos to begin close-range exploration.

stories.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
stories.summary: Researchers found that carrion crows make visual decisions about the direction of moving dots in an average of 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys, while maintaining high accuracy.
stories.finding: Researchers found that carrion crows make visual decisions about the direction of moving dots in an average of 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys, while maintaining high accuracy.
stories.significance: The study demonstrates that non-layered avian brains can process visual decisions using neural dynamics similar to primate brains, likely driven by evolutionary demands like flight and foraging.
stories.caveat: The exact biological mechanisms enabling crows to make visual decisions so much faster than primates remain unknown, and the behavioral experiment involved only two carrion crows.

stories.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
stories.summary: Researchers used a deep neural network to optimize electrical stimulation patterns for a visual cortex implant in a blind participant, predicting perceived flashes and shapes of light while using less electrical current.
stories.finding: Researchers used a deep neural network to optimize electrical stimulation patterns for a visual cortex implant in a blind participant, predicting perceived flashes and shapes of light while using less electrical current.
stories.significance: Brain implants that adapt to individual neural responses could bypass damaged eyes and optic nerves, moving closer to restoring reliable artificial vision.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover detected macromolecular organic carbon just a few microns below the surface of ancient mudstones in Mars' Bright Angel formation.
stories.finding: NASA's Perseverance rover detected macromolecular organic carbon just a few microns below the surface of ancient mudstones in Mars' Bright Angel formation.
stories.significance: Because similar organics were found thousands of miles away in Gale Crater, organic building blocks may have been widespread across ancient Martian lakes and rivers.

stories.title: A new treasure map reveals where Earth's lost prehistoric life may be hiding
stories.summary: An analysis of 540 million years of shallow marine fossils indicates that the greatest opportunities for discovering unknown prehistoric species exist in more recent periods, notably the Cenozoic Era, rather than the distant past.
stories.finding: An analysis of 540 million years of shallow marine fossils indicates that the greatest opportunities for discovering unknown prehistoric species exist in more recent periods, notably the Cenozoic Era, rather than the distant past.
stories.significance: Mapping unexplored areas with exposed, suitable geological strata allows paleontologists to strategically prioritize expeditions and museum collection reviews to expand the fossil record.
stories.caveat: Expanding the fossil record remains challenging and advances slowly, with fossilization itself preserving only a tiny fraction of Earth's past life.

stories.title: Euclid lays the foundation for its best-ever 3D map of the Universe
stories.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission published its DR1-Foundation dataset, cataloguing over 900 million galaxies, roughly 15,000 strong gravitational lens candidates, and spectra for over 160 million sources.
stories.finding: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission published its DR1-Foundation dataset, cataloguing over 900 million galaxies, roughly 15,000 strong gravitational lens candidates, and spectra for over 160 million sources.

stories.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water

stories.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5063-5069 Rocks and Chips

stories.title: Some PFAS chemicals are declining in English rivers but others are appearing

stories.title: Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought

stories.title: Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night

stories.title: Stone Age children left fingerprints on ancient art projects

stories.title: This magic mushroom can kill

stories.title: How a Metabolic Spark Could Have Jump-Started Life

stories.significance: Understanding the neurobiology and psychological priming behind sleep paralysis offers insights into consciousness, the mind-body connection, and potential cognitive techniques to reduce distressing episodes.
stories.caveat: The neurological explanations for why people see specific hallucinations remain theoretical, and the four-step intervention was tested in only six people.

stories.title: The Case for a Bubble at Life’s Start
stories.summary: The lipid-first model proposes that self-enclosed lipid bubbles served as initial compartments that could transmit compositional information and undergo natural selection prior to modern genetic systems.
stories.finding: The lipid-first model proposes that self-enclosed lipid bubbles served as initial compartments that could transmit compositional information and undergo natural selection prior to modern genetic systems.
stories.significance: Compartmentalization offers a solution to how dilute primordial chemical systems could concentrate reagents and undergo early evolutionary processes before the emergence of DNA or RNA.
stories.caveat: Critics point to an absence of experimental proof that lipid-only systems evolve, poorly understood prebiotic lipid synthesis, and analyses suggesting compositional replication is too inaccurate for selection.

stories.title: Science to restore speech is moving fast. Here’s what’s next
stories.summary: Brain-computer interfaces and decoding algorithms are advancing toward direct brain-to-voice translation, with recent testing reaching about 95 percent accuracy for listeners.
stories.finding: Brain-computer interfaces and decoding algorithms are advancing toward direct brain-to-voice translation, with recent testing reaching about 95 percent accuracy for listeners.
stories.significance: This technology enables paralyzed individuals who have lost the ability to speak to regain communication, potentially conducting faster and more natural conversations.
stories.caveat: Very few participants have received such speech-decoding implants to date, and current systems are still undergoing initial testing and require further refinement.

stories.title: Toxic secrets are hiding in Arctic ice

stories.significance: The findings quantify historical heavy metal emissions and demonstrate long-range atmospheric transport of industrial toxins from North America to polar regions.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Newly described insect may live its whole life on a spider’s web
stories.summary: Researchers have identified a newly described web-loving true bug species, Heissophila sinica, that may spend its entire life cycle residing directly on spider webs.
stories.finding: Researchers have identified a newly described web-loving true bug species, Heissophila sinica, that may spend its entire life cycle residing directly on spider webs.
stories.significance: The discovery sheds light on rare, specialized microhabitats and unusual symbiotic or commensal relationships between minute predatory insects and their arachnid hosts.
stories.caveat: Researchers are not yet sure whether the bugs primarily help or harm the host spiders, and precisely how they navigate the silk without sticking remains unclear.

stories.title: How neutrinos are beginning to reveal the secrets of our galaxy
stories.summary: IceCube researchers mapped the Milky Way using neutrinos and identified challenges in matching neutrino emission with high-energy light sources from the galactic centre.
stories.finding: IceCube researchers mapped the Milky Way using neutrinos and identified challenges in matching neutrino emission with high-energy light sources from the galactic centre.
stories.significance: Neutrinos offer a distinct observational window into cosmic phenomena and natural particle acceleration mechanisms that light alone cannot provide.
stories.caveat: Preprint / working paper; peer review is not established. Scientists face difficulties matching detected neutrino sources directly with known high-energy light sources under the assumption they share a common origin.

stories.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5056-5062: Charging Back Up!
stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover carried out an engineering test of activity parallelism by executing the CheMin data transfer simultaneously with an orbiter downlink communication window to conserve power.
stories.finding: NASA's Curiosity rover carried out an engineering test of activity parallelism by executing the CheMin data transfer simultaneously with an orbiter downlink communication window to conserve power.
stories.significance: As the rover's power output declines over time, parallel activity execution reduces awake time and operational energy consumption.
stories.caveat: The test appeared to go well, but the results remain to be analyzed and confirmed by the engineering team.

stories.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5050-5055: It’s Nazca, Our 49th Drill Hole
stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover successfully drilled its 49th Martian hole, named Nazca, targeting rock containing potential crystal inclusions, and delivered the sample to the CheMin instrument.
stories.finding: NASA's Curiosity rover successfully drilled its 49th Martian hole, named Nazca, targeting rock containing potential crystal inclusions, and delivered the sample to the CheMin instrument.
stories.significance: Analyzing rock containing potential crystal inclusions could help scientists reconstruct past environmental conditions on Mars by comparing them to Earth's geology.
stories.caveat: CheMin results have not yet been analyzed as data is still transmitting to Earth, and it remains unconfirmed whether the disc-shaped inclusions are actually crystals.

stories.title: Fossil fuel emissions are down in 2026. Green energy isn’t the reason
stories.summary: Scientists project that global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels will decrease by 0.4 percent in 2026, primarily driven by high oil prices from conflict rather than clean energy expansion.
stories.finding: Scientists project that global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels will decrease by 0.4 percent in 2026, primarily driven by high oil prices from conflict rather than clean energy expansion.
stories.significance: Renewable technologies counteract substantial emissions growth, but the clean energy transition must accelerate to produce sustained declines without relying on geopolitical energy shocks.
stories.caveat: The observed dip in fossil fuel emissions may be temporary and global emissions likely would have risen without the energy shock.

stories.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
stories.summary: Global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are projected to decrease by 0.4 percent in 2026, driven partly by an energy shock and oil price spike alongside renewable energy growth.
stories.finding: Global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are projected to decrease by 0.4 percent in 2026, driven partly by an energy shock and oil price spike alongside renewable energy growth.
stories.significance: This marks the first projected annual decline in global fossil fuel emissions in five years, influenced by high oil prices and the expansion of clean energy alternatives.
stories.caveat: The emissions decrease may only be a temporary blip, with researchers warning that emissions are likely to rebound if oil prices normalize before renewable energy accelerates enough.

stories.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
stories.summary: Researchers identified a gut-to-brain dopamine pathway concentrated in the left basolateral amygdala that drives learning to prefer specific flavors based on post-ingestive nutrient sensing.
stories.finding: Researchers identified a gut-to-brain dopamine pathway concentrated in the left basolateral amygdala that drives learning to prefer specific flavors based on post-ingestive nutrient sensing.
stories.significance: Understanding how gut nutrients teach the brain to enjoy initially unappealing flavors may inform new interventions to alter eating habits and food cravings.
stories.caveat: Why dopamine signaling is concentrated specifically on the left side of the brain remains unexplained, and potential links to GLP-1 drug actions remain untested hypotheses.

stories.title: Cold therapy may be worse than doing nothing for post-exercise recovery
stories.summary: Adults who used ice baths after intense leg exercise exhibited elevated markers of muscle damage for longer and regained less muscle strength than those who practiced passive rest.
stories.finding: Adults who used ice baths after intense leg exercise exhibited elevated markers of muscle damage for longer and regained less muscle strength than those who practiced passive rest.
stories.significance: The results challenge the popular practice of post-workout ice baths, suggesting they may delay muscle recovery rather than accelerate it.
stories.caveat: It remains unknown if outcomes differ with longer follow-ups, other exercise types, or modified interventions, and ice baths only temporarily masked pain.

stories.title: Drugs like Ozempic may help reverse chronic kidney disease
stories.summary: In patients with diabetic chronic kidney disease, semaglutide improved kidney blood flow, reduced scarring and vessel stiffness, and altered gene activity to suppress inflammation and activate repair.
stories.finding: In patients with diabetic chronic kidney disease, semaglutide improved kidney blood flow, reduced scarring and vessel stiffness, and altered gene activity to suppress inflammation and activate repair.
stories.significance: The findings explain how GLP-1 drugs directly protect and repair kidney blood vessels, offering a biological mechanism for their ability to slow kidney disease progression.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Did Life Begin in an RNA World?
stories.summary: Researchers identified a 45-nucleotide RNA molecule that can seize and copy another RNA strand, showing that self-replicating ribozymes do not necessarily require hundreds of linked nucleotides.
stories.finding: Researchers identified a 45-nucleotide RNA molecule that can seize and copy another RNA strand, showing that self-replicating ribozymes do not necessarily require hundreds of linked nucleotides.
stories.significance: Demonstrating that catalytic, self-replicating RNAs can be relatively small strengthens the plausibility that functional RNA sequences could have emerged by chance in a primordial prebiotic environment.
stories.caveat: It remains unknown if a suitable prebiotic niche existed on early Earth, and true living systems likely required more than genetic replication, such as metabolism.

stories.title: A high-fiber diet may clear away plastic in the gut
stories.summary: In mice fed plastic particles, consuming medium- or high-fiber diets helped clear more particles from the gut within 24 hours and prevented gut tissue damage seen in low-fiber mice.
stories.finding: In mice fed plastic particles, consuming medium- or high-fiber diets helped clear more particles from the gut within 24 hours and prevented gut tissue damage seen in low-fiber mice.
stories.significance: The results suggest that dietary fiber may offer a potential mechanism to trap ingested micro- and nanoplastics and shield gut tissue from damage.
stories.caveat: The research was conducted only in mice using fiber amounts far exceeding recommended human intake, and it is uncertain whether dietary fiber provides the same effect in people.

stories.title: Ozone Hole Reaches Its 2026 Maximum
stories.summary: The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh largest by area in 48 years of monitoring, driven by an unusually strong polar vortex.
stories.finding: The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh largest by area in 48 years of monitoring, driven by an unusually strong polar vortex.
stories.significance: Understanding annual fluctuations in ozone depletion helps track the long-term recovery of Earth's protective stratospheric layer following CFC phaseouts.
stories.caveat: Despite its substantial surface area, the 2026 ozone hole was not as deep as other large holes on record.

stories.title: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered
stories.summary: Scientists identified a new species of miniature killifish, named Laimosemion laranja, featuring distinct orange patterns and genetic divergence, discovered in the Rio Cajari drainage of northern Brazil.
stories.finding: Scientists identified a new species of miniature killifish, named Laimosemion laranja, featuring distinct orange patterns and genetic divergence, discovered in the Rio Cajari drainage of northern Brazil.
stories.significance: The discovery expands understanding of the diversity and evolutionary origins of annual life cycles within Amazonian killifish while drawing attention to poorly explored, vulnerable habitats.
stories.caveat: The species is known from only three small forest pools spanning an estimated 25 square kilometers, with all known sites experiencing environmental disruption from deforestation, mining, or urban pollution.
entities: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte

stories.title: Scientists wipe out deadly brain tumors in every mouse tested with new cancer therapy
stories.summary: Engineered B-SYNC CAR-T cells that activate specifically upon sensing brevican in the brain completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma tumors in two mouse models and persisted to prevent cancer recurrence.
stories.finding: Engineered B-SYNC CAR-T cells that activate specifically upon sensing brevican in the brain completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma tumors in two mouse models and persisted to prevent cancer recurrence.
stories.significance: Diffuse midline glioma is an aggressive, typically fatal childhood brain cancer; spatially restricting CAR-T activation may improve efficacy and reduce side effects compared to conventional therapies.
stories.caveat: The therapy has only been tested in preclinical mouse models and has not yet been evaluated for safety or effectiveness in humans.

stories.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
stories.summary: Fossils from Colombia's Paja Formation reveal an ancient marine ecosystem where declining older lineages coexisted with emerging newer lineages, demonstrating that major evolutionary transitions can happen without mass extinctions.
stories.finding: Fossils from Colombia's Paja Formation reveal an ancient marine ecosystem where declining older lineages coexisted with emerging newer lineages, demonstrating that major evolutionary transitions can happen without mass extinctions.
stories.significance: The pattern, termed a Biotic Inflection, suggests major biological transformations can be driven by high biodiversity and complex ecosystems rather than catastrophic die-offs.
stories.caveat: Researchers note that more evidence, including additional fossil finds and improved age estimates, is necessary to determine how common biotic inflections were throughout Earth's history.

stories.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
stories.summary: By measuring shot noise with scanning tunneling microscopy in a cuprate superconductor, researchers detected electron pairing occurring at the pseudogap energy scale.
stories.finding: By measuring shot noise with scanning tunneling microscopy in a cuprate superconductor, researchers detected electron pairing occurring at the pseudogap energy scale.
stories.significance: The evidence supports the idea that electron pairing can occur prior to the onset of phase coherence, potentially opening avenues to increase superconducting transition temperatures.
stories.caveat: The technique loses sensitivity at higher temperatures, preventing measurements above the superconducting transition temperature where the pseudogap typically appears, and it does not fully rule out entangled charge patterns.

stories.title: A nuclear blast could save Earth from an asteroid, but there's a catch
stories.summary: Simulations reveal that an asteroid's irregular shape significantly alters its response to a nuclear X-ray blast, causing deflection velocity to vary nearly fivefold based on blast direction.
stories.finding: Simulations reveal that an asteroid's irregular shape significantly alters its response to a nuclear X-ray blast, causing deflection velocity to vary nearly fivefold based on blast direction.
stories.significance: Understanding shape-dependent deflection allows planetary defense planners to optimize blast targeting and avoid inefficient redirection or unpredictable changes in asteroid spin.
stories.caveat: The current model only simulates the breakup of surface rocks and cannot accurately predict the potential fragmentation of an entire asteroid body.

stories.title: Ancient Siberian tomb reveals surprising secrets of cannabis use 2,800 years ago
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered roughly 1,000 cannabis seeds and chemical traces of cannabinoids in preserved human hair inside a 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb, indicating ancient Scythians used the plant for psychoactive effects.
stories.finding: Archaeologists discovered roughly 1,000 cannabis seeds and chemical traces of cannabinoids in preserved human hair inside a 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb, indicating ancient Scythians used the plant for psychoactive effects.
stories.significance: This discovery offers the oldest directly dated archaeological evidence for psychoactive cannabis use and provides insight into prehistoric funerary rituals and plant use.
stories.caveat: The findings cannot determine the amount consumed, the plant's THC potency, whether it was deliberately cultivated for psychoactivity, or the exact method of consumption.

stories.title: APOD: 2026 November 8 – Major Fireball Meteor
stories.summary: A major fireball meteor tracked over Germany was consistent with originating near the radiant of the Northern Taurid Meteor Shower, which is linked to dust from Encke's comet.
stories.finding: A major fireball meteor tracked over Germany was consistent with originating near the radiant of the Northern Taurid Meteor Shower, which is linked to dust from Encke's comet.
